title: Check the engine version at client startup
summary: Whenever the client is about to call the engine, it first verifies the engine: a missing engine produces a message that names the engine and the concrete install command, an engine below the declared minimum produces a message that names the required version and the concrete upgrade command, and a compatible engine proceeds normally. Reporting the client's own version and the declared requirement is exempt from this check and works without an engine, so a bare `executable not found` failure is never the outcome of a command that needs the engine.
plan_goal: Make Forgel and Forgel Code install and run as one working pair: give the engine `forgel` its own installer, add a mode of the Forgel Code installer that installs both binaries together (offered by default in the README, idempotent — when the engine is already present it compares versions and installs only a strictly newer one), and introduce a declared minimum supported engine version for Forgel Code, checked at startup, so a missing or too-old engine produces a clear actionable message instead of `engine forgel: executable not found: forgel`.

review.summary: The attributed change adds a new module `forgel_code/compat.py` with version parsing, action messages and a `confirm` helper, but nothing wires it into the client: neither `forgel_code/cli.py` nor `forgel_code/interactive.py` imports it or calls `confirm`, so no engine version is ever requested and none of the missing/too-old/unconfirmed behaviours reach the user. The client's version report in `cli.py` still prints only `forgel-code <version>` and never the declared minimum engine version, and no test exercises the confirmation path. The file itself is reasonably written, but in the repository's current state the feature the task asks for is not implemented — only an unused helper exists.

feedback: Do not rewrite or delete `forgel_code/compat.py` — it is already committed and its parsing, messages and `confirm` helper are accepted as they are. Start directly from the edit sites instead of re-reading the whole specification and repository.

In `forgel_code/cli.py`, call `compat.confirm(engine)` once, before the first engine-backed operation of the invocation, pass the confirmed version through the rest of the invocation, and never request the version a second time; do not confirm for the usage-help and version-report paths, which must stay engine-free.

Fail the invocation from that confirmation result: a missing or unstartable engine, an engine below the declared minimum and an engine whose answer carries no usable version must each end the command with the module's single actionable message and a non-zero exit, and must not attempt the requested operation. Reuse the client's existing failure path so the machine-readable form carries the same message and non-zero exit.
Change the client's version report so it prints both the client version and the single declared minimum engine version, and keeps exiting zero with no engine installed.

In `forgel_code/interactive.py`, perform the same confirmation before opening the prompt and exit non-zero with the actionable message instead of starting a session when the engine is missing, too old or unconfirmable.

Add tests that drive the confirmation through the real entry points with a stand-in engine: missing engine, engine below the minimum, engine answering without a usable version, and a supported engine proceeding unchanged; cover the version report showing the minimum and the interactive session's non-zero exit.
Report only what the diff actually contains: this attempt must end with the entry points, the version report and the tests present in the change set, not with a single unreferenced module.
